name: Tomato
source: ICAR Horticulture Handbook / FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29
notes: Prefers well-drained loam; sensitive to waterlogging and high EC (>1.5 dS/m).

name: Wheat
notes: Tolerant of a fairly wide pH band; responds well to split N application; moderate salinity tolerance.

name: Rice (Paddy)
notes: Tolerates slightly acidic pH; needs standing water for most of the season; sensitive to drought during panicle initiation.

name: Cotton
notes: Reasonably tolerant of moderate salinity/EC (up to 3.0 dS/m) and alkaline soils compared with vegetables.

name: Soybean
notes: Legume - fixes atmospheric nitrogen via rhizobium symbiosis; highly responsive to phosphorus and biofertilizer inoculation.

name: Onion
notes: Shallow-rooted and highly sensitive to salinity (EC > 1.2 dS/m); thrives best in high organic-carbon soils.

name: Sugarcane
notes: Long-duration, heavy feeder crop; requires high nutrient and water availability; susceptible to water stress.

name: Chickpea (Gram)
notes: Deep taproot; drought hardy with low water requirements; excess nitrogen causes vegetative lodging.

name: Mustard
notes: High sulphur requirement for glucosinolate oil synthesis; responsive to gypsum/elemental sulphur.

name: Groundnut
notes: Requires loose soil texture for peg penetration; requires calcium (gypsum) at pegging to prevent hollow pods.

name: Maize
notes: High nitrogen demanding C4 cereal; sensitive to waterlogging during early seedling stages.

name: Potato
notes: Tolerates slightly acidic soil (reduces common scab); strictly avoid MOP (use SOP to protect tuber dry matter).
